findings.title: Pre-existing comment now describes the wrong constant after LISTING_CONCURRENCY was inserted above LISTING_TTL_ENV
findings.suggested_fix: Move the new '#: Manifests fetched at once...' docstring-comment and the LISTING_CONCURRENCY assignment (lines 60-62) above the '# How long a listing may be stale...' comment, so that comment again sits directly over LISTING_TTL_ENV/DEFAULT_LISTING_TTL_SECONDS which it actually explains.

findings.title: Four new tunables are read once at import time, unlike every other env-driven setting in these modules, which is read per call
findings.suggested_fix: Read NGIAB_MAX_CONCURRENT_INGESTS, NGIAB_JOB_STALE_SECONDS (ingest.py:59), NGIAB_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY (ingest.py:50) and NGIAB_LISTING_CONCURRENCY (run_store.py:62) through a small function the same way local_root() (run_store.py:88), runs_prefix() (run_store.py:110) and listing_ttl_seconds() (run_store.py:341) already do, so a config change takes effect without a worker restart -- or note explicitly in each docstring that these four are deliberately import-time and why that differs from the others.

findings.title: ingest.py reaches into run_store's private _delete_prefix instead of a public API
findings.suggested_fix: run_store.py already has an internal caller of _delete_prefix at line 470 (delete_run); with ingest.py now a second, cross-module caller, drop the leading underscore (or add a thin public delete_prefix wrapper) in run_store.py and remove the '# noqa: SLF001' suppression in ingest.py rather than suppressing the lint that is flagging real API-boundary coupling.

findings.title: Job-concurrency state (_running, IngestBusy, _reap, _launch, MAX_CONCURRENT_INGESTS) lives in the HTTP controller module instead of ingest.py, which owns everything else about a job
findings.suggested_fix: Move _running, _reap, _launch, MAX_CONCURRENT_INGESTS and IngestBusy into ingest.py alongside IngestError, PENDING/RUNNING/DONE/FAILED, write_status and publish, and have controllers.py call a single ingest.start(...) that raises ingest.IngestBusy. This also removes the need for tests/test_job_lifecycle.py's autouse fixture (lines 43-46) to reach into controllers._running to reset module state between tests -- a sign the state is domain state, not request-handling state.

findings.title: Four new environment variables are undocumented, deepening an already undocumented pile of NGIAB_* knobs
findings.suggested_fix: README.md documents only NGIAB_STORAGE_BACKEND and mentions NGIAB_SCAN_ROOTS in passing; NGIAB_MANAGED_ROOT, NGIAB_RUNS_PREFIX and NGIAB_LISTING_TTL_SECONDS were already undocumented before this commit, and it adds NGIAB_MAX_CONCURRENT_INGESTS, NGIAB_JOB_STALE_SECONDS, NGIAB_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY and NGIAB_LISTING_CONCURRENCY on top with no new README section. Worth a single 'Tuning' table listing all of them with defaults before the count grows further.

findings.title: Two near-identical bounded ThreadPoolExecutor fan-outs (listing manifests, uploading a run) are not shared
findings.suggested_fix: run_store._cached_listing (line 392, pool.map, no partial-failure cleanup needed) and ingest._upload_directory (line 302, submit+drain-then-raise-first-failure, with cleanup on error) differ enough in failure handling that a shared helper may not pay for itself yet; if a third bounded fan-out shows up, factor a 'run bounded, wait for all, raise first failure' helper rather than duplicating a third time.

findings.title: IngestBusy is defined in controllers.py while its sibling IngestError lives in ingest.py
findings.suggested_fix: Define IngestBusy next to IngestError in ingest.py (both are raised by the ingest pipeline's launch/run step) and import it in controllers.py, matching the archive.ArchiveRejected / ingest.IngestError convention of each module owning its own domain exceptions.

residual_risks: MAX_CONCURRENT_INGESTS, UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY and LISTING_CONCURRENCY are process-local (controllers.py:455-459, ingest.py:50). Under multiple uvicorn/gunicorn workers the effective host-wide ceiling is MAX_CONCURRENT_INGESTS times the worker count, not the single number an operator sets. The docstring at controllers.py:455-458 acknowledges this ('Per worker process') but an operator reading only the env var name could still be surprised.

STALE_AFTER_SECONDS (ingest.py:59) is read once at import; changing NGIAB_JOB_STALE_SECONDS on a long-lived worker will not take effect until the worker restarts, which could leave a genuinely-stuck job unreported as failed for longer than an operator expects after they've just lowered the threshold to investigate one.
testing_gaps: No test exercises NGIAB_LISTING_CONCURRENCY, NGIAB_UPLOAD_CONCURRENCY or NGIAB_MAX_CONCURRENT_INGESTS being read from the environment itself (tests monkeypatch the already-parsed module constants, e.g. tests/test_job_lifecycle.py:91,109), so a typo in the env var name or a parsing regression (e.g. a non-numeric value) at import time would only surface as an app-wide startup failure, not a targeted test failure.
